stories.title: Microsoft opens up Xbox Cloud Gaming with new pay-as-you-go option

The change is set to roll out in November and targets infrequent cloud gaming users.

stories.title: Four major AI models suffer rare overlapping downtime
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Four prominent AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini) experienced simultaneous service interruptions.
The event highlights potential systemic vulnerabilities or shared infrastructure issues across leading AI platforms.
The rare overlapping downtime suggests a significant, albeit temporary, operational challenge in the AI industry.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) for high-level competitive programming tasks (e.g., IOI, ICPC).
A specialized pipeline combining problem curation, synthetic reasoning traces, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL) was developed.
The study compares performance between models trained with full SFT+RL versus those trained only with SFT on a dataset of 22,000 curated problems.

stories.title: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security
stories.author: James Mickens
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'linguistic illegibility' to describe when LLM outputs don't reflect internal model computation.
Highlights the unreliability of using externalized language artifacts or mechanistic probes to understand how LLMs truly function.
Addresses a fundamental security and interpretability challenge in large language models.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: Researchers developed an end-to-end pipeline (curation, synthetic traces, SFT, RL) to specialize LLMs for competitive programming.
The study trained two models, Nemotron-3-Nano-CC (using SFT+RL) and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC (using SFT only), on 22,000 curated problems.
The research directly addresses the challenge of testing LLM reasoning capabilities in high-stakes environments like IOI and ICPC.

stories.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
stories.author: Xiaodong Gu
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) agents.
Introduces 'EarlyEval' and 'early outcome prediction' as a method to reduce evaluation expenses.
Offers a complementary approach to existing benchmark distillation techniques.

stories.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
stories.author: Zheng Liu
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between autonomous AI agents and practical, domain-specific operational knowledge.
The proposed method, 'Repo-To-Skill,' aims to distill practical knowledge embedded in GitHub repositories into usable AI skills.
This work is crucial for advancing AI4AI systems by bridging the gap between theoretical ML methods and their practical, executable implementation.

stories.title: Qwen 3.8 27B available on Cerebras at 1500 tokens/s

The event relates to Tesla's focus on AI, autonomous vehicles, and future robotics.

bullet_points: TikTok reportedly withdrew from a congressional roundtable.

stories.title: Microsoft slashes Xbox Cloud Gaming to just 15 hours a month for Ultimate subscribers
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is significantly reducing the cloud gaming allowance for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers.
The unlimited cloud gaming feature, available across Game Pass tiers for the past year, is being capped.
Subscribers will now be limited to only 15 hours of Xbox Cloud Gaming per month starting in November.

stories.title: Xbox imposes harsh new time limits for Game Pass game streaming
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Xbox is introducing new, stricter time limits for Game Pass game streaming.
Subscribers who heavily utilize the streaming feature will face increased costs.
The change impacts over one million Game Pass subscribers.

stories.title: Just like a fruit fly, a new algorithm never forgets old scents
stories.author: Federica Sgorbissa
bullet_points: A new algorithm inspired by insect learning mechanisms has been developed.
The technique utilizes 'sparse coding' to enable fast learning in AI models.
A key feature of this algorithm is its ability to avoid 'catastrophic forgetting' when learning new information.

stories.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
stories.author: Roei Herzig
bullet_points: Current web agents utilize world models for action selection by predicting future web states.
These models are typically trained using supervised next-state prediction, generating fixed state representations (e.g., HTML snapshots).
The training objective (next-state prediction) is noted as being misaligned with the downstream ranker, which requires discriminative state representations.

stories.title: Towards Trustworthy Autonomous Robots: An Explainable AI-Based Decision Framework
stories.author: Cagri Temel
bullet_points: Addresses the critical auditability challenge in deep learning-powered autonomous robots.
Introduces TRACE (Transparent Reasoning Architecture for Credible Execution) as a solution.
The framework ensures every robot action can be traced back to sensor evidence via documented causal chains across four auditable layers.

stories.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
stories.author: Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the difficulty of Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in complex 5G/6G telecom networks due to cross-layer dependencies.
It highlights the limitations of using vanilla Large Language Models (LLMs) for telecom RCA, specifically mentioning hallucination and unstable reasoning.
The research proposes a structured reasoning framework to improve LLM performance and ensure evidence-grounded diagnosis in network operations.

stories.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
stories.author: Suproteem Sarkar
bullet_points: The research investigates the coherence of probabilistic forecasts generated by large language models (LLMs).
It addresses the growing trend of users relying on LLMs for complex, life-altering decisions that require probabilistic predictions.
The evaluation methodology builds upon de Finetti's theorem to test the internal consistency of the models' world views.

stories.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
stories.author: Dongrui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SafeEvolve, a novel approach for safety alignment in LLM-based agents.
Addresses the dual safety risks arising from both harmful final responses and unsafe multi-step execution trajectories.
Proposes a co-evolutionary method that jointly shapes the base model and the interaction harness using agent experience.

stories.title: Measurement-Driven Sub-Network Selection for On-Premise Retrieval-Augmented Factory Agents
stories.author: Athanasios Bachoumis
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of deploying large language models (LLMs) for on-premise factory agents due to hardware constraints.
Proposes a novel approach where model size is decoupled from adapted answer quality through structural compression and retrieval-grounded adaptation.
Reconceptualizes deployment as a post-adaptation selection problem, suggesting that general capability and retrieval quality are not solely dictated by parameter count.

stories.title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
stories.author: Oiwi Parker Jones
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical issue in Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs): the lack of a standardized metric for progress.
Speech BCIs are vital for restoring speech in individuals with paralysis and advancing human-computer interaction.
The variability in datasets, recording methods, and vocabularies prevents current BCI performance scores from being easily comparable.

stories.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
stories.author: Roei Herzig
bullet_points: Current web agents utilize world models for action selection by predicting future web states.
These models are often trained using supervised next-state prediction, yielding fixed representations (e.g., HTML snapshots).
The training objective is noted as being misaligned with the downstream ranker, which requires discriminative state predictions.

stories.title: Graph Machine: Towards Better Pretraining via Edges
stories.author: Lintai Hou
bullet_points: Introduces Graph Machine (GM), a novel architecture designed to improve pretraining methods.
GM maintains an $O(n)$-sized state accessible via sparse, dynamic routing, overcoming limitations of fixed-size states.
The core innovation involves using differentiable, pointer-like 'edges' for state access, replacing a significant portion of dense Transformer layers.

stories.title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
stories.author: Alessio Spurio Mancini
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical bottleneck in scientific computing: obtaining fast, exact gradients for ODE ensembles running on GPUs.
Current GPU solvers present a trade-off, where fast solvers lack efficient reverse-mode differentiation, and differentiable solvers are slow.
The proposed method, GRADSOLVE, aims to resolve this conflict by providing fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles.

stories.title: Improved Gradient Descent Lower Bounds Beyond Nesterov
stories.author: Kaizhao Liu
bullet_points: The research improves theoretical lower bounds for gradient descent acceleration in smooth convex optimization.
It establishes a new non-anytime lower bound of $\Omega(n^{-1.6342})$ and an anytime lower bound of $\Omega(n^{-1.2408})$.
These results surpass previous state-of-the-art lower bounds established by Ma and Chen and Tsai et al.

stories.title: UE5M3 FP4 Block Scaling for Stable Language Model Pretraining
stories.author: Paul Balanca
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of 4-bit floating-point (FP4) pretraining in language models due to limited magnitude range.
The proposed solution replaces standard E2M1 payloads with unsigned E5M3 block scales to achieve a wider dynamic range.
The new recipe allows for periodic tensor scaling, offering an alternative to existing methods like NVIDIA's Transformer Engine recipe.

stories.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
stories.author: Omri Abend
bullet_points: The research proposes that naturally occurring user feedback is a highly actionable learning signal for LLMs.
It challenges the current view that user feedback is inherently too noisy or difficult to leverage.
The study suggests that perceived ineffectiveness of user feedback is due to systematic biases in existing evaluation paradigms.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) for competitive programming, a rigorous test of AI reasoning.
A specialized pipeline combining problem curation, synthetic traces, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL) is introduced.
The study trains specialized models (Nemotron-3-Nano-CC and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC) to achieve high performance in coding competitions.

stories.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
stories.author: Suproteem Sarkar
bullet_points: The research investigates the coherence of probabilistic forecasts generated by language models (LLMs).
It addresses the growing user reliance on LLMs for high-stakes life decisions (e.g., economic or disaster predictions).
The evaluation method builds upon de Finetti's theorem to test the underlying 'world model' consistency of the models.

stories.title: DiscoSign: Discourse-Aware Text to Sign Language Gloss Translation
stories.author: Colin Lea
bullet_points: Introduces DiscoSign, a new computational approach for text-to-sign language gloss translation.
The system is designed to be discourse-aware, addressing limitations of traditional sentence-level processing in sign language.
It utilizes a modular Large Language Model (LLM) framework to handle complex linguistic phenomena like spatial coreference resolution.

stories.title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
stories.author: Jun Yu
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for continuous video stream processing.
Proposes 'ShallowStream,' a method that indexes shallowly before performing deep analysis for streaming video understanding.
Highlights the critical real-world applications of efficient streaming video understanding, such as autonomous driving and industrial monitoring.

stories.title: HyperStyler: Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer via Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks
stories.author: Chiehyeon Lim
bullet_points: Introduces 'HyperStyler' for Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer (LAST), allowing text rewriting with minimal author examples.
Addresses limitations in existing methods, specifically the averaging effect of static author embeddings which lose context-dependent style variation.
Proposes a novel approach using Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks to better control style while preserving semantic meaning.

stories.title: Untangling the Mechanisms of Misleading Context in Medical Question Answering
stories.author: Noémie Elhadad
bullet_points: Investigates how misleading context can corrupt the expert-level medical judgment of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The research examines the model's susceptibility to context, reasoning mechanisms, and decision monitorability.
Evaluations are conducted using the MedMisBench dataset, focusing on medical question answering.

bullet_points: The story reports on the successful flight of Y6, described as the world's largest electric aircraft.
This news falls under the broader category of sustainable aviation and electric propulsion technology.
